Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

inspire verb

fill with a feeling or the will to act

also inspiration, inspiring, inspired, inspire confidence, inspire hope, inspire fear

classical

Cic. Att. 3.22.1: spem (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Verr. 2.3.68: alicui formīdinem (Lewis & Short)

injiciō, injicere, injēcī, injectum

verb, third conjugation, transitive; the feeling in the accusative, the person in the dative · Conjugation on Wiktionary

put into, inspire (a feeling in someone)

Lewis & Short: “to bring into, inspire, infuse”. Its first sense is to throw in or on; with a feeling it says what the feeling is: spem injicere, inspire hope; metum injicere, inspire fear.

Other words

  • īnflammō, īnflammāre, īnflammāvī, īnflammātum — fire, kindle (with eagerness)

    verb, first conjugation, transitive; ad + acc. or the abl. · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 1.7.9: ā pueritiā īnflammātus ad glōriam (Lewis & Short); Cic. Lael. 86: īnflammārī cupiditāte honōrum (Lewis & Short) · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    Inspire as setting someone on fire for something; literally, to set alight.

  • afflātus, afflātūs m. — inspiration (from a god)

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Cic. N.D. 2.167: nēmō vir magnus sine aliquō afflātū dīvīnō umquam fuit (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    A breath or blast; in Cicero the breath of a god in a great man or an orator.

  • īnspīrō, īnspīrāre, īnspīrāvī, īnspīrātum — breathe into; inspire (a feeling); in Christian Latin, inspire

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Verg. A. 6.12: magnam mentem animumque (Lewis & Short); Vulg. 2 Pet. 1.21: Spīritū Sānctō (Lewis & Short) · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    (vōx plērumque poētica: Verg.; in ōrātiōne solūtā post Augustum (Quint., Curt.))

    Poetic and post-Augustan (Lewis & Short); the word of the Vulgate for inspiration by the Holy Spirit, and so of church life.

Examples

  • nēmō vir magnus sine aliquō afflātū dīvīnō umquam fuit

    no man was ever great without some divine inspirationCic. N.D. 2.167 (Lewis & Short)

See also encourage, encourage, excite.
